title: Designing Intuitive Bilingual Interfaces: Internationalization Best Practices
summary: Why text expansion in French and German breaks rigid button layouts and how to build adaptive Flexbox containers.
content:
When designing interfaces that seamlessly toggle between English and French (EN/FR), layout overflow is the number one defect. French translations typically expand string length by 20% to 30% compared to English equivalents.

### Designing for Text Expansion
Avoid hardcoded width classes on buttons, cards, or pills (`w-32`). Instead, use `white-space: nowrap`, `padding`, and flexible inline containers that scale with content gracefully.

```html
<!-- Bad: Fixed width button causes text overflow in French -->
<button class="w-24 text-sm truncate">Send Message</button>

<!-- Good: Flexible padding and whitespace isolation -->
<button class="px-6 py-3 whitespace-nowrap text-sm font-semibold hover:bg-opacity-90">
  Envoyer le message
</button>
```

### Key Principles
1. Store all user-facing strings in lightweight, structured JSON files.
2. Maintain consistent key names across language files to prevent fallback glitches.
3. Test diacritic characters and uppercase typography (`font-label-caps`) in all screen sizes.
